pamphlet_excerpts: Dietary Sources of Calcium: Calcium is found in dairy products such as milk, cheese, and yogurt, and foods such as nuts, beans, broccoli, and canned salmon (p. 7).
Daily Calcium for Bones: Making sure you have at least four servings of calcium daily will help ensure that your bones stay strong throughout your life (p. 7).
Preventing Future Osteoporosis Risks: If you do not get enough calcium in your diet while you are young, you could be at risk for the bone-thinning disease called osteoporosis (p. 7).
Consequences of Poor Fueling: Failing to fuel and refuel your body with good foods can lead to fatigue and injury; you will also be more likely to getsick (p. 7).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Consume Enough Daily Calcium: If you do not get enough calcium in your diet while you are young, you could be at risk for the bone-thinning disease called osteoporosis (p. 7).
Step 2 - Fuel and Refuel Properly: Failing to fuel and refuel your body with good foods can lead to fatigue and injury; you will also be more likely to getsick (p. 7).
Step 3 - Build Lifelong Eating Habits: Develop good eating habits now so that they will become second nature to you throughout your lifetime (p. 7).
Step 4 - Consult Related Fitness Resources: For more information about nutrition and physical fitness, read the Cooking and Personal Fitness merit badge pamphlets (p. 7).
